pages.lesson:
LESSON: MULTIPLICATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.2: Multiplication

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Multiplication
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: When can you use multiplication in real life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. Multiply up to a two-digit number by multiples of 10
2. Multiply up to a two-digit number by a two-digit number, with and without regrouping
3. Multiply up to a two-digit number by 100
4. Estimate products by rounding to the nearest 10
5. Create multiplication patterns with products not more than 100

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ What multiplication means

• Multiplication is repeated addition.
• 4 × 3 means 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
• Kenya uses: market prices, equal rows of desks, garden plots.

▸ Multiply by multiples of 10

Teach
• Multiply the non-zero parts, then add the zero(s) from the multiple of 10.

Worked example
• 24 × 10 → 24 × 1 = 24, add one zero → 240.
• 36 × 20 → 36 × 2 = 72, add one zero → 720.
• 45 × 30 → 45 × 3 = 135, add one zero → 1,350.

Try this
• 16 × 10
• 25 × 20
• 33 × 30
• (Check later: 160; 500; 990)

▸ Two-digit × two-digit (break-up method)

Teach
• Break the second number into tens + ones.
• Multiply each part, then add.

Worked example
• 23 × 14
• 14 = 10 + 4
• 23 × 10 = 230
• 23 × 4 = 92
• 230 + 92 = 322

Try this
• 12 × 13
• 27 × 15
• (Check later: 156; 405)

▸ Multiply by 100

Teach
• Write the number, then add two zeros.

Worked example
• 18 × 100 = 1,800
• 42 × 100 = 4,200

Try this
• 7 × 100
• 35 × 100
• (Check later: 700; 3,500)

▸ Estimate by rounding to 10

Teach
• Round each factor to the nearest 10.
• Multiply the rounded numbers.

Worked example
• Estimate 48 × 19
• 48 → 50, 19 → 20
• 50 × 20 = 1,000 (estimate)

Try this
• Estimate 34 × 22
• (Check later: about 600 (30 × 20))


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• 24 × 10 = 240
• 23 × 14 = 322
• 18 × 100 = 1,800
• 48 × 19 ≈ 1,000

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Work out: 16 × 10, 25 × 20, 33 × 30.
2. Work out: 23 × 14 and 27 × 15. Show break-up.
3. Work out: 18 × 100 and 42 × 100.
4. Estimate: 48 × 19 and 34 × 22.
5. Word problem: One book costs KSh 35. Cost of 10 books?

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Write and solve 10 mixed multiplication questions in your book.
2. Make a ×12 chart from 12 × 1 to 12 × 10.
3. Invent one market word problem and solve it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When can you use multiplication in real life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• ×10 → add one zero; ×100 → add two zeros.
• Break 2-digit multipliers into tens + ones.
• Estimate by rounding to 10, then multiply.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
